title: Testing Components
summary: Write unit tests with TestBed and Vitest: render a component, set signal inputs, click buttons, await whenStable, replace services with fakes and test HTTP calls with HttpTestingController.
introduction: Angular projects come with a test runner configured: since Angular 21 the CLI uses Vitest, and ng test runs every spec file in the project. Testing a component means rendering it in a TestBed, poking at the DOM and checking what appears, which also forces you to keep components small and services replaceable. This lesson tests a counter component, a service and an API class, and shows the one timing rule that trips up most beginners in zoneless tests.
learningObjectives: Render a component with TestBed, set inputs with setInput and query the DOM
Trigger events and wait for rendering with whenStable before asserting
Test a service directly and an HttpClient call with HttpTestingController

blocks.text: Every file ending in `.spec.ts` is a test file. `ng generate component` creates one next to each component, and `ng test` runs them all with Vitest in a browser-like environment. `describe`, `it`, `expect` and `beforeEach` are available globally, so a spec needs no imports beyond Angular's `TestBed` and the class under test.

items: `TestBed.configureTestingModule` sets up a tiny application for the test; `imports` lists the component under test, `providers` can replace services.
`createComponent` returns a **fixture**: a handle on the component instance (`componentInstance`), its host element (`nativeElement`) and rendering (`whenStable`).
`fixture.componentRef.setInput('label', 'Clicks')` sets a signal input the way a parent template would. Assigning to `componentInstance.label` does not work because inputs are read-only signals.
`await fixture.whenStable()` waits until Angular has rendered everything pending. Query the DOM after it, never before.

blocks.title: Common mistake: asserting before Angular has rendered
blocks.text: In a zoneless app a click schedules a render; it does not happen synchronously inside `click()`. Remove the second `await fixture.whenStable()` and the test reads the old DOM and fails with `AssertionError: expected 'Count: 0' to be 'Count: 1'`. The rule: after creating the component, after setting an input and after any event, `await fixture.whenStable()` before you look at the DOM. `fixture.detectChanges()` also works for a synchronous check, but `whenStable` additionally waits for pending effects and resources.

blocks.text: Services with no DOM are the easiest things to test: ask the injector for an instance and call its methods. `TestBed.inject` returns the same singleton the components would get, created fresh for each test because the TestBed is reset between tests.

blocks.text: Replacing a service with a fake

A component that injects `CartService` should be tested without the real cart logic. Provide an object with just the members the component uses; since the template reads signals, the fake exposes signals too. This is dependency injection paying for itself.

blocks.text: `provideHttpClientTesting()` swaps the real backend for a controller that records requests. The test subscribes, checks that exactly one request went to the expected URL, answers it with `flush`, and finally calls `verify()` to make sure no unexpected requests were made.

blocks.text: Test behaviour the user can observe rather than implementation details: assert on rendered text, not on private fields. Vitest's `vi.fn()` and `vi.spyOn()` from the `vitest` package create spies when you need to assert that a fake method was called. `ng test --coverage` reports which lines ran; aim for meaningful tests on logic and templates rather than a percentage.

blocks.title: End-to-end tests
blocks.text: Unit tests cover one component at a time. For a flow such as *log in, add to cart, check out* use a browser automation tool like [Playwright](/tutorials/playwright) or [Cypress](/tutorials/cypress) against the running app. The [Vitest tutorial](/tutorials/vitest) covers the runner's own features in depth.

questions.question: How do you give a component's `readonly label = input('Count')` the value `'Clicks'` in a test?
questions.explanation: Signal inputs are read-only from inside the component; the fixture's `componentRef.setInput` sets them the way a parent would.

questions.question: `http.verify()` fails the test if a request was made that the test did not expect.
questions.explanation: `verify()` asserts that no unmatched requests remain, which catches accidental extra calls.
